header:
Problem 9 Prins Cyclization (25 points, 12%)
The Prins cyclization is a powerful synthetic transformation that rapidly constructs tetrahydropyran rings. Tetrahydropyran is a common structural unit in many bioactive molecules, including spongistatins and bryostatins. Researchers have used the Prins cyclization in numerous elegant strategies for the total synthesis of natural-product targets.

9.2 A key advantage of the Prins cyclization is that, starting from a single stereocenter and a defined alkene geometry, it can construct up to four stereocenters on a tetrahydropyran ring with high stereoselectivity. In some cases, however, enantiomeric excess (ee) is lost.
9.2.1 In the Prins cyclization below, the ee of the major product is lower than that of the starting material, and small amounts of two byproducts are detected.
Predict the configurations of the chiral carbons in the product by assigning the absolute configurations of chiral carbons a and b in the major product using S/R notation.

text_images.description: Single-step reaction: 'O[C@H](CC=C)C1=CC=CC=C1' reacts with PhCH2CH2CHO under BF3·OEt2 and AcOH conditions to give the major product, 'O=C(O[C@H]1C[C@@H](CCC2=CC=CC=C2)O[C@@H](C3=CC=CC=C3)C1)C', byproduct 1, 'O=C(OC1CC(C2=CC=CC=C2)OC(C3=CC=CC=C3)C1)C', and byproduct 2, 'O=C(OC1CC(CCC2=CC=CC=C2)OC(CCC3=CC=CC=C3)C1)C'. Starting material M is labeled 87% ee and the major product 67% ee. Chiral carbons a and b are labeled on the ring of the major product; OAc at a is shown on a solid wedge, while CH2CH2Ph at b is shown on a dashed bond.
